business_summary.text: ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company is India's second-largest AMC by quarterly average AUM, managing mutual funds, PMS, AIFs and advisory mandates.

call_points.text: FY27 ESOP cost guidance maintained at ₹64-68 Cr, charged pro-rata.
Alternates net yield expected to stay in the 90-100 bps range.
Systematic transactions moderated to ₹4,672 Cr from ₹4,872 Cr in June.
Acquisition of ICICI Securities PMS business adds ~₹3,000 Cr AUM.
Redemptions are slightly higher in current market conditions.
SIF portfolio scaled to ₹4,948 Cr from ₹2,678 Cr in Q1.
Advisory AUM declining due to international FII outflows.
Management remains conservative on mid-cap valuations, favoring large-caps.

capital_actions.instrument: Bonus and share split (restated dividend per share)

operating_notes.text: SEBI settlement order SO/AS/PSD/2026-27/8680 dated 16 April 2026 closed the tenure-extension matter of ICICI Prudential Venture Capital Fund – Real Estate Scheme – I, with ₹14,35,500 paid as settlement amount.
FY26 fees and commission expense was ₹4,192.3 Cr against revenue from operations of ₹5,764.6 Cr.
The company paid interim dividends of ₹2,640.4 Cr in FY26 and proposed a final dividend of ₹12.40 per share.
The company acquired investment management rights of identified Category II AIFs from ICICI Venture for ₹1,079.4 million, effective April 1, 2026.
FY26 revenue from ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund was ₹4,841.4 Cr, the only customer above 10% of total revenue of ₹5,764.6 Cr.
FY26 trademark licence fee to ICICI Bank was ₹265.1 Cr (FY25 ₹205.0 Cr); dividend paid to ICICI Bank ₹1,361.3 Cr and to Prudential Corporation Holdings ₹1,188.0 Cr.
FY26 interim dividend paid was ₹2,640.4 Cr; a final dividend of ₹12.40 per share is proposed for shareholder approval.
SEBI issued an administrative warning letter regarding a procedural delay in investor eligibility verification in an AIF scheme, with no material financial impact.
Equity margins were 66 bps annualised, debt 32 bps, liquid and passive 12 bps each and arbitrage 30 bps in Q1FY27.
Industry June 2026 SIP contribution was ₹31,781 Cr; ICICI Pru's June systematic transactions were ₹4,872 Cr versus ₹5,104 Cr in March 2026.
Alternates quarterly average AUM was ₹79,446 Cr, with PMS at ₹28,996 Cr and AIF at ₹22,737 Cr; gross yield 1.91% and net yield 0.95%.
Alternates AUM stood at ₹80,965 Cr as of Sep-2026.
SIF quarterly average AUM reached ₹4,948 Cr in Q2FY27.

timeline.summary: On 20 April 2026 ICICI Prudential AMC disclosed a SEBI settlement order dated 16 April 2026, with ₹14.36 lakh paid, closing the matter of the tenure extension of ICICI Prudential Venture Capital Fund – Real Estate Scheme – I.
Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹1,517.01 Cr, net profit ₹763.42 Cr.

On 29 May 2026 ICICI Prudential AMC filed the notice of its 33rd AGM (24 June 2026) with the FY26 annual report: unmodified audit opinion, ₹12.40 final dividend, FY26 revenue ₹5,764.6 Cr and profit ₹3,298.3 Cr.
On 3 June 2026, ICICI Prudential AMC disclosed that SEBI issued an administrative warning letter on May 25, 2026, regarding a procedural delay in investor eligibility verification for an AIF scheme.
ICICI Pru AMC reported Q2FY27 operating profit of ₹1,181 Cr and declared an interim dividend of ₹30 per share.

upcoming_events.description: Record date for FY26 final dividend of ₹12.40 per share
33rd Annual General Meeting through VC/OAVM at 2.30 p.m. IST

status_history.evidence: Final dividend of ₹12.40 per share for FY26 is placed before shareholders at the 33rd AGM on 24 June 2026; approval pending.

watchlist.text: Shareholder approval of the FY26 final dividend at the AGM
Revenue from ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund as share of total revenue
Shareholders' approval of appointment of Mr. Prashant Kumar as Independent Director and Mr. Rajeev Mittal as Non-Executive Director
Shareholders' approval of remuneration revisions for Mr. Nimesh Shah and Mr. Sankaran Naren
Shareholders' approval of M/s. Parikh & Associates as Secretarial Auditors for five years

status_history.evidence: Systematic transactions moderated to ₹4,672 Cr from ₹4,872 Cr in June.

watchlist.response: Naveen Agarwal said the company only discloses total systematic transactions and advised looking at quarterly rather than monthly numbers; Nimesh Shah said the scheme data was too dispersed to share
watchlist.text: Analysts repeatedly asked for quarterly SIP flows and scheme-wise SIP mix; management gave only the June monthly systematic figure of ₹4,872 Cr

watchlist.response: Naveen Agarwal said the June and March distribution mixes were largely unchanged and questioned whether the analyst was looking at industry numbers
watchlist.text: Rahil Shah (HSBC) asked why bank-channel AUM fell while direct and national distributors grew; he said he would take it offline after management pointed to the equity AUM base

watchlist.response: Naveen Agarwal said about 50% is seed capital and promised to revert separately on the AIF/REIT MTM split, which was not answered on the call
watchlist.text: Shreyas Pimple (Nomura) asked how much of the ₹4,225 Cr investment book, including 23.5% in AIF/other equity/REIT, is mark-to-market exposed

watchlist.response: Naveen Agarwal said the company does not give future guidance and called the current quarter the right run-rate base
watchlist.text: Prayesh Jain (Motilal Oswal) asked for FY27 opex and employee cost outlook
Regulatory approvals for PMS business acquisition from ICICI Securities

watchlist.response: Attributed to investor shift toward small/mid-cap strategies and pre-emption of STPs into lump sum during market corrections.
watchlist.text: Decline in systematic transaction (SIP/STP) book compared to industry growth.

watchlist.response: Efforts continue across all channels; bank channel strategy depends on their own distribution priorities.
watchlist.text: Stagnant AUM growth from the ICICI Bank channel.
